gaps.lead: It's very unlikely that Martin will win the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.sentence: Martin has almost ___ the 100 metres, as he's out of training.
gaps.explanation: 'It's very unlikely he will win' becomes 'he has almost no chance of winning'.

gaps.lead: Although he is remarkably rich, he lives very simply.
gaps.explanation: Although he may be rich → Rich as (he) may be — fronted adjective + as + may.

gaps.lead: The party was incredibly boring, so we left early.
gaps.sentence: The party was ___ we left early.

gaps.lead: She'll be on a flight, so she can't join the call.
gaps.sentence: She'll be on a flight, so ___ join the call.
gaps.explanation: won't be able to = future inability.

gaps.lead: She speaks French better than her brother does.
gaps.explanation: 'Doesn't speak French as well as' reverses the comparison.

gaps.lead: Assembling the wardrobe took me two hours.
gaps.explanation: it took me X to do = I spent X doing.
